title: Change event (v1) — one item of the /v1/changes feed
description:
One event of the public change feed, the sync primitive for integrators who would otherwise poll every artifact (TRN-046). The feed is stored as append-only segments plus a meta document, and the read route pages with a cursor that is the last-seen event ULID; `next` is always present, so a poller that is caught up idles on 304s rather than on empty pages (FS10-070/071). Feed page envelope: `{ "items": [ <this schema> ], "next": "evt_…" }` — see the OpenAPI description.

PERSONAL DATA: NONE. Every payload field is P0-public registry state (FS-00 §6.9). That is a structural property of the event catalogue below, not a filter applied on the way out.

Phase: P-M4, demand-gated. The schema is published now so that an integrator building against this contract set can see the shape it will get, and so the feed can be switched on without a schema change (FS-00 §6.10).

vsRefs: (not in the P-M2 build sheet — P-M2 §5 item 20)

id.description: Event ULID — sortable, which is what makes it usable as the feed cursor (FS-00 §6.1, FS10-071).

type.description: The complete event catalogue (FS10-070). Additive-only: a new type may be added, an existing one never redefined (WEB-112).

payload.description: Type-dependent, P0-public fields only. The `allOf` rules below state the minimum each type carries; additional P0 fields may be added additively.
payload.$comment: Deliberately open (additionalProperties permitted) so an additive P0 field does not require a new schema version. What is NOT permitted is any personal datum: emails, names of individuals, and money amounts attributable to a person never appear in this feed (FS-00 §6.9, D15).

githubNodeId.description: A GitHub GraphQL node_id, in either of the two forms GitHub has issued: the opaque current form (a repository's is `R_`-prefixed) and the legacy base64 form, whose decoded value begins `010:Repository` and whose `=` padding the first alternative cannot express. Widened 2026-09-08 to admit the second: `registry-v0-record.v1` accepts both, so a record the curated registry accepts is publishable in this artifact. The primary key for repositories and people throughout this contract set (FS-00 §6.1).
